topic: whether social media accounts should require age verification
instructions: address the reader directly as 'you' at least twice
include one deliberate sentence fragment for emphasis
repeat one chosen phrase at the start of two different paragraphs
close with a single-sentence call to action
use an em-dash-free, semicolon-free punctuation style
write the final paragraph in second person throughout
text:
Social media companies have failed to protect their youngest users from online predators and cyberbullying.

You can't ignore the statistics: children as young as eight are using social media platforms, and it's no wonder that these apps are designed to be addictive. But while some argue that this is just a natural part of growing up in the digital age, I firmly believe that social media accounts should require age verification before allowing users under the age of 16 onto their platform.

Children need to be protected from online harm; that's why we have laws regulating child labor and protection from exploitation. Social media companies are effectively operating in a regulatory gray area, profiting from the data they collect while doing little to safeguard their youngest customers. By not requiring age verification, these companies are essentially leaving the door open for predators and bullies.

The risks are real: without age verification, social media platforms become breeding grounds for harassment, grooming, and exploitation. And yet, you may ask, what about the teenagers who insist on using social media despite their parents' best efforts to keep them off? (As if that's an excuse to turn a blind eye to the dangers these apps pose.)

To require age verification would be a major turning point for the industry; it would force companies like Facebook and Instagram to re-evaluate their business model, one that currently relies heavily on user data. But it's time to put profits over users – we need to prioritize our children's safety above all else.

You have a responsibility as a parent or guardian to protect your child from online harm; but you also have the power to demand more from social media companies. It's time to hold them accountable for their role in facilitating exploitation and harassment. Demand age verification on social media platforms now!
